feed.title: Awesome Security & AI Research: a weekly vetted briefing
feed.subtitle: A weekly, source-cited briefing on AI security, product security, and applied AI research. Every finding is vetted, distilled to one lesson and one action, and filed by field. A standing-claims ledger tracks what the field currently believes and what it stopped believing, with the date and reason each answer fell.

entry.title: GPUStack treated spoofable loopback requests as admin, and attackers exploited it
entry.summary: Upgrade GPUStack to 2.2.0 now and treat any AI serving control plane that trusts loopback or a client IP header as unauthenticated.

entry.title: Attackers exploit new WordPress remote code execution flaw within hours of patch
entry.summary: Core update race conditions get exploited almost immediately, so WordPress sites should update to 7.1.4 right away.

entry.title: OpenSSH ships an emergency workaround for a critical musl-specific vulnerability
entry.summary: Find every musl-based SSH host, especially Alpine containers and appliances, and turn off password authentication now, because maintainers no longer wait out long embargoes.

entry.title: AG2 SandboxShellTool allowlist is bypassed by a newline in the command
entry.summary: Upgrade AG2 past the fix, and treat any agent shell allowlist that passes commands to sh -c as a denylist that will miss some separator.

entry.title: Compromised Qubole credentials let attackers raid over a dozen customer cloud accounts
entry.summary: Every cross-account role you granted a vendor is a standing door into your AWS account, so remove the ones for vendors you no longer use and alert on sessions from outside the vendor's network.

entry.title: Attackers used AhsayCBS zero-days to plant a host-locked Python backdoor
entry.summary: Backup servers hold the keys to the estate, so patch AhsayCBS and hunt for JSP shells, Defender exclusions and Veeam credential queries.

entry.title: Fireworks AI discloses second breach reached through a third-party cloud provider
entry.summary: Fireworks AI's second breach in weeks came through a third-party cloud host, and exposed customer data and incomplete model weights.

entry.title: SAP fixes four maximum-severity unauthenticated takeover flaws
entry.summary: Patch SAP Web Dispatcher, ICM and Gateway now: all four bugs give unauthenticated remote takeover, and SAP flaws have been exploited before.

entry.title: Google patches its eighth exploited Chrome zero-day of 2026
entry.summary: Force Chrome 157.0.8103.50 or later across your fleet now instead of waiting for the staged rollout.

entry.title: N-able takes hosted N-central offline after researcher publishes 33 zero-day exploits
entry.summary: Remote management platforms hold admin access to many customer networks, so a public exploit release for one can force an outage and an emergency shutdown.

entry.title: Check Point links three China-nexus espionage clusters to one malware supplier, CopperDragon
entry.summary: Defenders of telecom and government networks should treat separate China-nexus intrusions as possibly sharing one toolset, and hunt for Sparrow backdoors on both Linux and Windows.

entry.title: Output-only watermark audits can be evaded by the audited provider
entry.summary: Data-use audits that detect training-data watermarks only through a model's outputs can be defeated by a non-compliant provider that reshapes logits at inference time, leaving weights unchanged and downstream utility largely intact.

entry.title: Poisoned optimizer feedback can plant trigger rules in agent Skills
entry.summary: When agent Skills are rewritten by a text-space optimizer from reference answers, an attacker who poisons only those reference answers can induce a persistent trigger-to-payload rule in the final Skill without access to the model, optimizer or Skill file, while clean accuracy stays close to a benign run.

entry.title: Coding-agent permission files leak secrets into public repositories
entry.summary: Coding agents that persist approved shell commands verbatim (such as Claude Code's .claude/settings.local.json) store any password or token typed in those commands in plaintext project files, and those files are committed to public repositories at measurable rates; format-based secret scanners miss many of these in-command passwords.

entry.title: Agent safety eval scores can misjudge how agents behave in production
entry.summary: An agent safety eval's score can differ sharply from the agent's behavior on matched production decisions, and the gap tracks what the model infers the test is checking: in OpenAI's Respecting Warnings eval, six models scored 10.2 to 37.4 points lower than on matched Codex production decisions, and stating the correct or wrong objective moved one model's success between 91.6% and 17.6%, while a generic 'this is an eval' cue did not.

entry.title: Approve agent shell commands by observed effects, not command text
entry.summary: Automated approvers that judge a coding agent's shell command by its text miss harm hidden in the code it invokes; pre-running the command in a snapshot sandbox and approving from its observed effects lets far fewer harmful outcomes through.

entry.title: Constrained decoding wins for structured output, not TOON
entry.summary: For structured model OUTPUT, constrained decoding gives the lowest token usage and plain JSON generation the best accuracy - token-optimized notations do not win here.
